clue.text: Country person's nice large shed

indicators.note: to shed something is to cast it off, so the letter for the size word is dropped

blocks.note: nice means agreeable
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A rural dweller owns a pleasant, roomy outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a noun for a garden hut, but it is a verb: PLEASANT sheds its L to leave PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a farm labourer or smallholder who lives in the countryside.

clue.text: Glad prisoner's first let out

indicators.note: first picks out only the leading letter of the inmate word

blocks.note: the initial letter of the word
to let out property is to rent or lease it

explanation.surface: A happy inmate was released at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let out' suggests release from jail, but it is the landlord's sense of renting.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleased means happy and satisfied, a direct synonym for glad.

clue.text: Exploits groom in Ascot

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and rearrange, so the letters are restyled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a stable lad at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is a famous English racecourse, which makes groom look like a stable hand; 'in' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploits as a noun are daring deeds, which are actions.

clue.text: Get older set of books for broker

blocks.note: to age is to grow older
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An ageing accountant sorts the ledgers for a stockbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker acts for others in a deal, which is what an agent does.

clue.text: Medical care each time maiden's stuck in river

indicators.note: stuck in means wedged inside, so the run of letters goes into the river name

blocks.note: the Trent is a major English river
ea is the abbreviation for each
T is the abbreviation for time
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl trapped in a river needs urgent medical attention every time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent flows through the English Midlands; the three short pieces sit together inside it, in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the care given by a doctor to cure an illness or injury.

clue.text: Is almost anxious after learner pays attention

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word for anxious is lost

blocks.note: L is the learner plate on a car
taken as written
anxious means nervous, on edge

explanation.surface: A nervous student driver concentrates hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after learner' is a placement instruction: the pieces built from 'Is almost anxious' follow the L.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to heed what is being said, which is a synonym for paying attention.

clue.text: This makes pal drink

blocks.note: surface reading: something that creates friendship over a drink
setter's reading: the answer's first word written upwards, as in a down light, spells pal

explanation.surface: A shared drink turns a stranger into a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Read upwards, LAP gives PAL, so LAP UP 'makes pal'; the phrase also means drink greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does with milk.

clue.text: Joints had better get rest on a regular basis

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: you had better means you should
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Aching joints ought to be rested regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is not a link: its letters join those of 'rest' in the alternate selection.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoulders are the ball-and-socket joints connecting the arms to the torso.

clue.text: Stylish necklace ultimately on social worker

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the jewellery word is used

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
on is the leg side in cricket
ants are social insects, and workers in the colony

explanation.surface: A smart necklace finally ends up on a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and leg side are the same half of the field. 'social worker' is not a caseworker but an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, a synonym for stylish.

clue.text: Meet female model going north in state

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means travelling upwards, so the letters read in reverse
in puts the reversed letters inside the word for state

blocks.note: to state is to say
F is the abbreviation for female
to model for an artist is to sit

explanation.surface: A woman posing for an artist travels north to meet someone in another state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' reverses both the female letter and the model word together before they go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a demand or need is to satisfy it, fulfil it.

clue.text: Desperate former lover getting married with spruce clothing?

indicators.note: clothing wraps around the body, so the tree word is placed around the letter for married

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a spruce is a kind of tree
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A frantic ex-partner gets wed in smart attire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spruce' reads as smart, but it is the conifer, which wraps round M.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate measures are drastic ones, so the word for going to the utmost limit matches.

clue.text: Argue in favour of exam

blocks.note: pro means for, in support of
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A student makes the case for keeping an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to object or argue against something, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Baseball fielder's two items of clothing

blocks.note: first garment: short trousers
second garment: an upper-body garment

explanation.surface: A ballplayer's uniform consists of a couple of garments.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase supplies both garments, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The shortstop is the infield player positioned between second and third base.

clue.text: Boys crossing over mountains

indicators.note: the boys straddle the letter, crossing over it so it sits between them

blocks.note: lads are boys
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Young lads hike across a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mountains' is not peaks but the informal sense of a great heap, as in mountains of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads and mountains are both colloquial words for large quantities.

clue.text: Dance music is constant in party

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word for party

blocks.note: a do is a party
taken as written
C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: At the party the dance tunes never stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Disco is a genre of upbeat dance music popular in the 1970s.

clue.text: A chorister unfortunately ignores current group of musicians

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order
to ignore is to leave out, so the letter standing for current is dropped

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A choir singer sadly snubs the present band.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of instrumental players.

clue.text: Really awful men let in Yemen's capital

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are rearranged
a capital is a head or leading letter, so only the opening one is kept

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
taken as written for the mix
the initial letter of the country

explanation.surface: Men were admitted to the Yemeni capital, and it was truly dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is part of the anagram fodder, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminently means to a notable degree, highly, which is an intensifier like really.

clue.text: Crooked dice – and it showed!

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of true, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Loaded dice gave the cheating away!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked dice' reads as rigged gambling, but crooked just bends the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate is to point out or show, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Loyal cadet died fighting

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scuffle that throws everything into disarray

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A faithful young soldier fell in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedicated means committed and devoted, which is a close synonym for faithful.

clue.text: Determined group of detectives intercepting legal document

indicators.note: to intercept is to come between, so the detectives cut into the document

blocks.note: a deed is a legal document
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: Resolute police officers seize a legal paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Decided can mean resolved or settled, and also unwavering, matching determined.

clue.text: Takes ecstasy during car journeys?

indicators.note: during places the drug letter within the span of the trips word

blocks.note: drives are trips by car
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone pops pills while out on road trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes ecstasy' looks like the drug habit; 'Takes' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To derive something is to take or obtain it from a source.

clue.text: Clear up wine after change of heart

indicators.note: a change swaps one letter out for another, here at the centre of the word

blocks.note: Soave is a dry white Italian wine
the new central letter that replaces the old heart; the clue leaves it to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away the wine after rethinking things.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not name the replacement letter, so the definition and crossings must fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a mystery is to solve it, find its answer.

clue.text: More fleet-footed match substitute?

blocks.note: first meaning: ... on one's feet, more nimble
second meaning: a device used instead of a match to make a flame

explanation.surface: A quicker player comes on as a replacement in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a sports substitution; the match is the one you strike.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of light means nimbler, and a cigarette lighter replaces a match.

clue.text: Old tree with ugly half removed

indicators.note: half removed means one half is taken away, so only the back two letters stay

blocks.note: the elder is a shrub or small tree
the second half of the word

explanation.surface: An old tree, partly felled, looks hideous.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly means advanced in years, a gentler word for old.

clue.text: Torment worthless dogs with little energy

blocks.note: curs are mongrels or low-grade dogs
E is the abbreviation for energy, little meaning short form

explanation.surface: Mangy mongrels with no vigour are a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A curse is an affliction or scourge, something that torments a person.

clue.text: Even nan coughed, badly lacking oxygen

indicators.note: badly says the letters are put together poorly, in a jumbled order
lacking means going without, so the element letter is taken away

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Grandma coughed badly even without an oxygen supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb opening the sentence, but it is the definition, meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Something even stays constant and level, just as something unchanged stays the same.

clue.text: Part of lower steering apparatus on vessel heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the head goes, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: a rudder steers a boat

explanation.surface: A section of the lower steering gear on a ship is missing its front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lower' is not 'further down' but a cow, an animal that lows; a rudder is found on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's udder is the milk-producing organ hanging from its belly.

clue.text: US president is mad and somewhat upsetting

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the run of words is used
upsetting means tipping up, so in a down clue the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: the letters running across the gap between words

explanation.surface: An American president is crazy and rather distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'is mad and' backwards gives dnadamsi, which holds the name.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and his son John Quincy Adams were the second and sixth presidents of the USA.

clue.text: Edward turned over and suggested getting affectionate

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the short name is read the other way

blocks.note: Ed is short for Edward
to vote can mean to propose, as in 'I vote we leave'

explanation.surface: Edward rolled over and made a proposal, becoming loving.
explanation.definitionFit: Devoted means deeply loving and loyal, a synonym for affectionate.

clue.text: Farm vehicle followed the woman, as Cockney said

indicators.note: said points to speech, and a Cockney drops the h and the final r of her

blocks.note: followed = tracked, the woman = her, which a Cockney says as 'er

explanation.surface: A tractor trailed a lady, as an East Londoner put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class accent of East London, which drops the h at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is the powerful motor vehicle used to pull farm machinery.

clue.text: Some Parisian couple's hopelessness

blocks.note: des is French for some
a couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A couple from Paris is in a state of gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Initially digs expose secret ancient city's ruin

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the initial letters of these three words
Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: Archaeological digs reveal the hidden ruins of an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to wreck it, which is the verb sense of ruin.
